reports.lens: LONG-SAMPLE EDGE: whether TZA or a -3x Russell 2000 position has a lasting open-to-close edge, and whether the +1% take-profit with a 15:49 exit has positive expectancy outside the Sep-Oct 2026 run. Data: TZA daily bars 2008-11-06 to 2026-10-13 (4,509 sessions). IWM daily bars 2000-05-26 to 2026-10-13 (6,633 sessions), used to build a synthetic -3x IWM with daily reset (1.08%/yr expense ratio deducted). SPXS, SQQQ, SOXS and NVDQ daily bars, used to replicate the instrument ranking. TZA 1-minute bars and trades.csv, used for calibration.
key_findings: There is no lasting open-to-close edge. TZA 2008-2026 averages -0.057%/day open to close (sd 3.72, median -0.144, win 47.7%, skew +0.01, t -1.03, n=4509). The synthetic -3x IWM 2000-2026 averages +0.018%/day (t +0.39, n=6631). IWM's own open-to-close mean is -0.007%/day; its return is overnight (+0.068%/day). Small caps have no intraday down-drift for a -3x position to harvest. TZA's open-to-close mean was positive in only 8 of 18 full years, the synthetic's in 14 of 27.

The +1% take-profit rule (TP) has negative expectancy over the long sample. Entry is assumed at open+0.1%; the TP counts as hit if the day's high reaches entry*1.01, otherwise exit at the close. On those assumptions TZA averages -0.162%/day (t -5.0, win 70%, skew -2.63), and positive years number 3 of 18. The synthetic averages -0.109%/day (t -4.1, skew -2.56), and positive years number 10 of 27, none significant. The conservative variant requires the high to reach entry*1.015. It gives TZA -0.432%/day and the synthetic -0.391%/day, and no year is positive in either series.

The TP does not create an edge; it only changes the shape of returns. With zero entry slippage the synthetic TP rule averages -0.009%/day, against +0.018% for holding to the close. That matches optional stopping on a series with near-zero drift: the TP buys a 70% win rate at the cost of skew around -2.5. No TP level from 0.5% to 2% is significantly positive on either series at any slippage. Over 2016-2026 with zero slippage the synthetic gives TP 1% +0.021%/day (t 0.5).

Trailing windows show the edge is recent only. On TZA the TP rule averages +0.607%/day over the last 30 sessions (t 3.5), +0.347% over 60 and +0.198% over 120. Over 250 sessions it is -0.146%, over 500 -0.127%, over 1000 -0.071% and over all 4509 -0.162%. The last-30 and last-60 TP means sit at the 98.9th and 99.0th percentiles of all rolling TZA windows. Only 14.4% of rolling 250-session TZA windows (24.2% of synthetic ones) have a positive TP-rule mean.

The current run is the regime, not the rule. IWM fell 5.9% over the last 30 sessions with 20-day realised vol of about 11% (10/13 close: below its 50- and 200-day averages, 50-day momentum -6.6%). A 30-session score (mean/sd) of 0.42 or more happens in only 0.8-0.9% of rolling windows. The episode that began 2026-09-17 has had 19 qualifying sessions, the longest such run in 26 years of synthetic data.

Trailing performance does not predict the next period. Across non-overlapping 30-session blocks, the correlation between one block's open-to-close mean and the next block's is -0.078 for the synthetic and -0.010 for TZA. After blocks averaging +0.6% or more, the next block's TP mean was -0.24% for the synthetic (12 of 36 positive) and -0.16% for TZA (5 of 13 positive). All 6 earlier TZA episodes with a score of 0.4 or more had a negative TP mean over the following 30 sessions (average about -0.41%/day); 8 of the 13 synthetic episodes did too.

The weekly ranking rule adds nothing. Picking the top trailing-30 score among TZA, SPXS, SQQQ, SOXS and NVDQ each week, then trading the TP rule, gave -0.183%/day (t -5.55, n=4137, 2010-2026). Always trading TZA gave -0.157%. Restricting to weeks where the top score was 0.3 or more gave -0.201% (n=192). A +0.67% 30-session mean happens by chance 16.8% of the time under iid resampling of the long-run synthetic, and about 60% of the time for the best of 5 roughly independent ETFs. The original pick of TZA is consistent with luck plus selection.

No regime filter rescues the TP rule. Every regime bucket gave a non-positive TP mean except 3 small synthetic buckets with t ≤ 1. The few open-to-close readings with t near 2 point the opposite way to the current story: synthetic +0.129% (t 2.6) when IWM is above both its 50- and 200-day averages; synthetic +0.114% (t 2.0) and TZA +0.109% (t 1.7) when IWM's 20-day vol is under 15%. The TP rule in those same buckets was -0.061%, -0.034% and -0.119%. When IWM is below its 50-day average, TZA averaged -0.191% open to close and -0.227% under the TP rule. Down-trends help TZA overnight, not intraday. Day of week makes no difference: the live Thu/Fri/Mon schedule gives TZA TP -0.187%, against -0.125% on Tue/Wed. With about 25 buckets tested, none survive a multiple-testing correction.

Daily-bar simulations still flatter live results. Over 21 sessions the optimistic daily-bar simulation matched the 1-minute simulation (18 vs 18 hits, +0.815% vs +0.823%). But on the 7 live legs since the TP went in (9/28-10/12), live averaged +0.469% with 4 hits, against +0.671% (5 hits) for the optimistic daily-bar simulation and +0.545% for the conservative one. Live entries averaged +0.21% above the open (+0.145% for 09:31 close + $0.01 on 1-minute bars), more than the 0.1% slippage assumed. The real fund also lags the synthetic by 0.044%/day (TZA minus synthetic, 2009-2026; -0.12%/day in 2020), so the synthetic flatters TZA.

The day leg carries real tail and drawdown risk. TP-rule days at -5% or worse happen about 10.4 times a year (TZA 186 of 4509; 12 in the last 250 sessions), and -3% or worse about 28 times a year. The worst TZA TP days were -22.7% (2008-11-26), -17.5% (2010-07-23) and -15.6% (2020-06-15). Simulating the day leg alone at 90% of equity on 3 of every 5 sessions, with the optimistic TP: over 60 sessions (36 legs) the median ending equity multiple is 0.95-0.96, the chance of finishing down is 64-68%, and the chance of a drawdown of 20% or more is about 15%. Over 250 sessions (150 legs) the median is 0.81-0.85, the chance of finishing down is 75-85%, and the chance of a 20% drawdown is about 79%. With the conservative TP the 60-session drawdown chance is about 31% and the 250-session median is 0.58.

recommended_changes: Suspend the day leg (RULES_v3 §11) by default. Over 26 years the -3x Russell 2000 open-to-close return is about zero before costs and negative after realistic entry costs. The +1% TP adds a 70% win rate and a skew of about -2.5, not expectancy. That tail feeds PAUSE risk directly.

Do not justify keeping it with the trailing-30 ranking score or a trend filter. Trailing scores do not predict the next period (block correlation about 0, after-episode TP means negative). The ranking replication lost money over 2010-2026. No regime bucket has a significant positive TP mean.

If the human still wants a small regime bet, set it up in advance as an experiment. Size it at no more than about 45% of equity (1 share). Set a fixed end date or a stop condition: for example, stop after N legs, or once cumulative live day-leg P&L since 10/13 goes negative. Judge it only on live fills, never on daily-bar backtests, which overstate live results by about 0.1-0.2%/leg.

If it is kept at any size, record each leg's 09:32 entry vs the open and the TP fill time. Live entries average +0.21% above the open, which on its own wipes out the long-run zero-slippage expectancy.
When suspended, leave the overnight leg's cash flow as it is. The 09:31 sale proceeds wait for the 15:52 entry. The PDT budget then stays free for emergency same-day exits.
caveats: The TP fill is inferred from daily bars, so the timing of the high relative to the 09:32 entry is unknown. The optimistic variant matched the 1-minute simulation on 21 sessions, but live hits (4 of 7) fell short of it (5 of 7).

The 0.1% entry slippage is an assumption, and the long-run drift from 09:30 to 09:32 is not measurable without long intraday data. With zero slippage the long-sample TP rule is about 0 (synthetic -0.009%/day, TZA -0.058%/day), still not positive.
The close is used in place of the 15:49 exit. Spreads and commissions on the exit are not modelled beyond the entry slippage.

The synthetic -3x IWM ignores swap and borrow costs beyond the 1.08% expense ratio. Real TZA lagged it by 0.044%/day, so the synthetic is optimistic. Early TZA (2009) tracked poorly, with a daily difference sd of 1.69%.
IWM bars before about 2004 show zero volume. Their OHLC looks consistent (no inconsistent bars, 85 opens equal to the prior close), but early open prices may be less reliable.

About 25 regime buckets were tested, so the t≈2 readings are not significant after a multiple-testing correction. There are few score-0.4 episodes (6 TZA, 13 synthetic), so the persistence evidence is directionally consistent but small-sample.
The compounding risk figures cover the day leg alone and use overlapping rolling windows, including the 2008 and 2020 crises. They are not a joint simulation with the overnight leg.

A short-term continuation signal is possible: the next-day TZA TP mean after a score of 0.4 or more was +0.377% (t 1.73, n=48). Those days are heavily clustered (6 episodes), and the 30-day forward return was negative in all 6 earlier episodes.

reports.lens: DOES THE 30-SESSION RANK PREDICT? This is a walk-forward test of the trailing-score instrument selection and of a trailing-mean regime filter for the TZA day leg. It uses 2 years of real daily bars for 10 inverse ETFs (2024-09-03..2026-10-13, 85 out-of-sample weeks) and 15.3 years of real ETF daily bars (2011-07..2026-10, 798 weeks; NVDQ is synthesized as -2x NVDA, its o->c correlates 0.996 with real NVDQ; LABD is excluded from the long run). Each week the #1 name by trailing-N open->close mean/sd is held open->close for every session, with returns as raw o->c, with the 1% take-profit rule on daily bars, and with the TP rule plus costs.
key_findings: Current reading reproduced: TZA trailing-30 o->c score was 0.45 as of 2026-10-09 (mean +0.78%, 22/30 up) and 0.41 as of 10-13. SPXS -0.02, NVDQ 0.06, SQQQ -0.19, SOXS -0.26.

Over the last 2 years the cross-sectional rank IC (Spearman of trailing score vs next-week mean o->c, 85 weekly obs, CORE5) is near zero at every lookback: N=10 -0.028 (t -0.47), N=30 +0.019 (t +0.33), N=60 +0.008 (t +0.15), N=120 +0.064 (t +1.14). The 10-ETF universe is similar, with all |t| < 0.5.

Over 15 years (798 weeks) the N=30 IC is +0.014 (t +0.76) for CORE5 and +0.015 (t +0.90) for ALL9. Only slower lookbacks show a faint relative signal: N=60 IC +0.054 (t +2.90), N=120 +0.035 (t +1.82). It never turns into positive absolute returns. N=60 pure #1 makes -0.047%/session vs always-TZA -0.009%. Against next-week TP returns the N=30 IC is +0.021 (t +1.11).

Holding the pure #1 does not beat always-TZA. Over 2 years, N=30 o->c gives -0.130%/session vs always-TZA -0.098%, the equal-weight basket -0.168% and cash 0; 36% of random weekly picks do as well. Over 15 years, N=30 #1 gives -0.100% o->c (t -1.63) and -0.077% with TP (t -2.18), vs always-TZA TP -0.010% (t -0.32).

The live configuration (CORE5, N=30, eligible only if mean>0, win>=50% and 60-session mean>0, else cash, with 1% TP) is the only bright spot in the 2-year window: +0.147%/session, t +2.87, positive in both halves. It looks like a lucky parameter. Neighbours are much weaker: N=25 +0.048, N=35 +0.077, N=20 +0.053, N=40 +0.032. With 0.2% entry and 0.1% exit cost it falls to +0.085% (t 1.47), while every neighbour is <= +0.008%.

The same live configuration over 15 years makes -0.030%/session (t -1.19), positive in only 6 of 16 years. With light costs it is -0.055% (t -2.15), and every lookback from N=20 to N=40 is negative. Of 714 rolling 85-week windows, the median t is -0.65, 24.5% are positive and only 1.1% reach t >= 2.0, all of them starting 2024-05..2025-03. Of 9 non-overlapping 85-week blocks, 8 are at or below +0.005%/session; only the latest is positive (+0.112%, t 1.55). The recent window that motivated the rule is the best stretch in 15 years.

TZA's own time-series signal points the wrong way for momentum. Over 15 years, Spearman of trailing-N score vs next-week o->c is N=30 rho -0.073 (t -2.07), N=60 -0.080 (t -2.26), N=120 -0.072 (t -2.04): mild mean reversion. Against TP returns it is about zero (N=30 -0.026, t -0.73).

The regime filter (trade TZA only when its trailing-N o->c mean > 0) is backwards over 15 years. On daily o->c, ON days vs OFF days: N=20 -0.123% vs +0.097% (Welch t -2.06), N=30 -0.134% vs +0.107% (t -2.25), N=60 -0.087% vs +0.060% (t -1.37). With TP: N=30 ON -0.046% vs OFF +0.024% (t -1.14), N=60 -0.006% vs -0.013% (t +0.12). In the last 2 years N=20 and N=30 are also backwards (TP N=30: -0.138% vs +0.106%, t -1.40). Only N=60 is positive there (+0.037% vs -0.046%, t +0.49), which is noise.

Today's high score is roughly the chance rate. TZA's own 30-score was >= 0.45 in 6 of 798 weeks. An iid bootstrap of TZA's 15-year o->c gives P(30-score >= 0.45) = 0.008 per window, about 6.4 weeks expected. In the 12 weeks where TZA ranked #1 with score >= 0.4 (54 sessions), the next week averaged -0.019%/session o->c and +0.202% with TP (t 0.66, but -0.405% with 0.2%/0.1% cost).

In the 2-year sample the positive live-config result splits into a selection part (active-week pick +0.385% vs the equal-weight basket -0.031% on the same days) and a cash-timing part. Over 15 years the selection value on active sessions shrinks to pick -0.074% vs basket -0.131% vs TZA -0.089% (pick minus basket t +1.27): the selection only chooses the least-bad of a set of negative-drift assets.

The daily-bar TP model is optimistic about entry. The 12 live entries averaged +0.209% above the official open (median +0.307%). 1-minute bars show open-to-09:32 drift of +0.141% (21 sessions, t 1.62). Always-TZA with TP and 0.2% in / 0.1% out is -0.243%/session over 15 years (t -7.17) and -0.197% over the last 2 years. Because the TP rule's edge sits in the first ~1% move, 0.15% of extra entry cost moves the 15-year mean from -0.070% to -0.243%.
Live day legs D01-D12 average +0.342%/leg (sd 0.928, t 1.27, n=12); the TP-era legs D07-D12 average +0.613%. This sample is too small to separate from the zero-mean base rate above.

recommended_changes: Suspend the day leg (§11). Neither the 30-session rank nor a trailing-mean filter gives out-of-sample evidence of a positive expected return. Without them the leg is unconditional TZA with TP: about -0.01%/session before costs over 15 years, and clearly negative at the measured ~0.2% entry drift. It still adds most of the short-horizon PAUSE risk.

Stop using the weekly inverse-ETF re-rank as evidence. Its out-of-sample IC is about zero at N=30 (2y t +0.33, 15y t +0.76). If the table is kept, label it informational only, as v1.5 already did for the overnight 30-night rank.
Do not adopt a trailing-mean>0 regime filter for TZA. Over 15 years it selects worse days (N=30 Welch t -2.25 on o->c).

If the human wants the leg kept as an experiment: fix the instrument to TZA (no rank switching) and cut size to about 40-50% of E to limit PAUSE risk. Pre-register a stop rule using realised returns measured from the actual 09:32 fill, e.g. drop the leg if after 20 TP-era legs the mean is < +0.15%/leg net. Note that n=12 so far gives t 1.27.

Any future TP backtest should model entry at the 09:32 price (open plus about 0.14-0.21% measured drift), not the official open. The TP rule's result is very sensitive to entry cost: in the 15-year sample, 0.15% of extra entry cost moves the mean by about -0.17%/session.
caveats: The 2024-07..2026-10 block is the only positive 85-week block in 15 years (+0.112%/session, t 1.55). A real regime shift (persistent small-cap intraday weakness) can't be ruled out, but it can't be told apart from the selection-on-recent-performance that produced the rule.

Daily-bar TP modelling assumes no stop and that the high is reachable after entry. It ignores highs printed in the first 2 minutes, so the no-cost TP numbers are optimistic. The cost variants are a flat approximation.

NVDQ before 2023-10 is synthetic: -2x NVDA, daily reset, no fees or premium. It ran +0.054%/day above real NVDQ over the 530-day overlap. 2010 bars were noisy (e.g. TECS +337% o->c on 2010-07-08), so the long sample starts 2011-01-03 with out-of-sample from 2011-07.

The universe is highly redundant (TZA/SRTY, SPXS/SDOW, SQQQ/TECS), so the effective number of independent bets per week is smaller than 5 or 10. IC t-stats use weekly non-overlapping forward windows, with a lag-1 autocorrelation adjustment that changed little.

The eligibility clause 'full-window mean>0' was interpreted as a trailing 60-session mean > 0. Dropping it, or using 64, changes the 2-year result (+0.156% active-session pick mean without the clause, +0.398% with N=64) but not the 15-year conclusion.
The PDT 3-of-5-days constraint was not simulated. It scales exposure and does not change per-session predictability.

reports.lens: JOINT RISK WITH THE OVERNIGHT LEG: a combined daily simulation (NVDL overnight at 0.89 of E, then the TZA TP-rule day leg 3 sessions in 5 on a rotating schedule). Circular block bootstrap, block 5, 5000 paths of 60 and 125 sessions from E0 = 104.6. PAUSE (<= 0.8 x rolling-20 end-of-day high, checked at 09:31 and at end of day): overnight drops to 1 NVDL share (36.58/E, about 35% of E0) and the day leg is skipped for 5 sessions. KILL at <= 50. Three datasets: A = the specified 1y file (257 sessions, real NVDL); B = real NVDL 2023-07..2026-10 (824 sessions; earlier NVDL opening prints are bad, and the 2023-12-27 distribution night is replaced by 2x NVDA); C = 2017-12..2026-10 (2226 sessions; synthetic 2x NVDA overnight minus 4bp, real TZA). Each is run under two day-leg execution scenarios: entry = open (optimistic), and entry = open +0.15% (realistic). Both include a 0.05% exit slip on non-TP days. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/wf2/joint-risk/ (prep.py, calib.py, stats.py, sim.py, extra.py, sweep.py, sim_out.txt, extra_out.txt, sweep_out.txt).
key_findings: Every day-leg size lowers expected log growth in all 3 datasets under both execution scenarios. Growth falls steadily as size rises; no size adds growth. On 1y data at 125 sessions, overnight-only is +0.312%/session. Adding the day leg gives +0.267/+0.195 at 90% of E (optimistic/realistic), +0.274/+0.212 under the current whole-share v1.4 rule, +0.294/+0.262 with 1 share, +0.290/+0.250 at 50%, +0.302/+0.282 at 25%, and +0.274/+0.258 with the trailing-30 gate.

The day leg is the main driver of short-horizon PAUSE risk. On 1y data, P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) is 5.1% overnight-only. It rises to 22.8% (optimistic) / 27.2% (realistic) at 90%, 18.6% / 22.0% under the current rule, 10.1% / 11.6% with 1 share, 7.0% / 7.5% at 25%, and 17.6% / 19.1% with the gate. Over 125 sessions it goes from 11.1% to 44.8% / 51.8% at 90%. On the 3.3y data it goes from 26.0% to 37.2% / 40.2%, and on the 8.8y data from 36.0% to 45.3% / 48.5%.

Terminal equity at 125 sessions on 1y data: median 155.0 overnight-only vs 146.4 / 133.6 at 90%; 5th percentile 102.6 vs 88.1 / 80.6. With 1 share the median is 151.8 / 145.4. On 8.8y data the median is 124.6 overnight-only vs 121.2 / 111.8 at 90%, and P(KILL within 125) is 0.8% vs 1.3% / 2.2%. P(KILL) is about 0 on 1y data for every variant.

P(reach 200 within 125 sessions) is 18.8% overnight-only on 1y data. The day leg at 90% raises it only under optimistic execution (20.9%; 3.3y data 24.5 vs 21.7; 8.8y data 11.3 vs 10.3). That gain comes from added variance, not edge. Under realistic execution it falls to 13.5% (1y), 18.1% (3.3y) and 7.7% (8.8y).

The day leg has no long-sample edge. TP-rule mean per active day, optimistic / realistic execution: 1y -0.063% / -0.199% (sd 2.1, skew about -1.8, 5th percentile about -5%); 3.3y -0.004% / -0.128%; 8.8y -0.024% / -0.148% (t = -3.29). Under realistic execution the mean is negative in every calendar year 2018-2026. Only the recent window is positive: last 30 sessions +0.64% / +0.62%, last 60 +0.33% / +0.29%. The first 197 sessions of the 1y file were -0.18% / -0.35%.

Execution calibration. On the 21 one-minute sessions, the daily-bar rule (entry = open) gives +0.84%; the 1m rule with entry at the 09:31 close gives +0.82%, and with entry at the 09:32 close +0.66%. On the 40 five-minute sessions it is +0.62% (daily rule) vs +0.48%. Live 09:3x fills averaged +0.21% above the daily open. Over the 7 legs since the TP rule started, live averaged +0.47% vs +0.71% for the daily model. So entry = open overstates the day leg by about 0.15-0.25%/day, which supports the +0.15% slip as the realistic scenario.

Hedge or amplifier: in the current regime the day leg amplifies the overnight leg. Same-day TZA open->close vs the preceding NVDL overnight return has correlation +0.155 on 1y data (block-bootstrap 90% CI +0.037..+0.267) and +0.121 on 3.3y data (CI +0.061..+0.178). The 8.8y synthetic gives +0.009 (CI -0.038..+0.054); synthetic C restricted to the 3.3y window gives +0.119, so the effect belongs to the 2023+ regime and is not a data artifact. The TP-rule day leg's correlation is +0.148 (1y) and +0.077 (3.3y). After the worst 10% of NVDL nights (<= -3.4%), the day leg averages -1.24% on 1y data (n=26) and -0.49% on 3.3y data: it loses on the same mornings the core has just lost. The correlation with the following overnight is about 0 (+0.014). The same-night TZA gap vs NVDL is -0.63, but the day leg never holds overnight, so that hedge is not captured.

Joint tails on 1y data, 0.89 overnight plus 0.90 day leg in one session: 1st percentile -5.67% overnight-only vs -9.20% combined; P(session <= -5%) 1.6% vs 7.4%; both legs below -2% on the same session 5.1% vs 3.2% if independent. Worst 5-session log return -11.9% vs -15.6%; 5th percentile 5-session -6.0% vs -9.8%. In variance terms, the day leg adds about 58% to the overnight leg's variance, and the covariance term is +12.5% of the combined variance.

The trailing-30 TZA open->close > 0 gate has no predictive power. Next-session day leg with the gate on vs off: 1y -0.208% vs -0.192%; 3.3y -0.125% vs -0.130%; 8.8y -0.168% vs -0.128%. Other gates tested on 8.8y data: trailing-30 TP-rule mean > 0 (-0.177 vs -0.136), trailing-60 (-0.125 vs -0.179), trailing-10 (-0.155 vs -0.145), and a score > 0.25 gate (+0.040%, n=125, about 1 se; not significant). After the 10 sessions in 8.8 years where TZA's trailing-30 score was >= 0.45 (the reason TZA was picked), the forward-30 day-leg mean was -0.28% / -0.60%; this sample is tiny.

Breakeven sweep (shift day-leg returns, 1y data, realistic execution). For the 90% leg to match overnight-only log growth the true day-leg mean must be at least about +0.03-0.05%/day: at 0% it gives 0.298 vs 0.312, at +0.1% 0.351. Even at the +0.3%/day §11 assumes, P(PAUSE within 60) is 16.5% vs 5.1%. On 8.8y data at +0.3%, growth is 0.267 vs 0.132 and P(PAUSE within 60) 39.6% vs 36.0%. The verdict therefore rests on whether the edge is real, and no long sample supports one.

The live record cannot settle it: 12 legs average +0.342% (sd 0.93, t = 1.27). Telling a +0.30% mean from 0 at a 2.1% day-leg sd needs about 303 legs (about 2 years at 3 per week), or about 69 even at sd 1.0.

In every dataset and both execution scenarios the day leg lowers expected log growth and median and 5th-percentile terminal equity. It raises 60-session P(PAUSE) about 4-5x on 1y data (5.1% to 22.8-27.2%), and on the 8.8y data P(KILL within 125) rises from 0.8% to 1.3-2.2%.

If the human wants to keep the day leg as a live experiment, cap it at exactly 1 TZA share (about 46% of E at $48.26 / $104.6) and drop the v1.4 top-up to 2 shares. On 1y data that holds 60-session P(PAUSE) to 10.1-11.6% and costs about 0.02-0.05%/session of log growth, against 0.04-0.12% at 90%.

Do not adopt the trailing-30 open->close > 0 gate. It does not predict next-session day-leg returns (1y on/off -0.208%/-0.192%; 8.8y -0.168%/-0.128%). Its only effect in the simulation is running the leg on fewer days.
Do not plan on a 25%-of-E leg: whole shares cannot do it until E is about $193 (one TZA share is about 46% of E today). Use 1 share or off.

Set a re-entry criterion now, before seeing more data: resume only when at least 250 sessions of the TP rule on TZA at executable prices (09:32 entry, not the open) show a mean > +0.10%/day, and the joint bootstrap shows 60-session P(PAUSE) no more than 5 points above overnight-only. The 12-leg live sample (t = 1.27) and the 30-session score (0.45) cannot discriminate: about 300 legs are needed.
With the day leg suspended, the 15:52 overnight entry no longer depends on the 15:49 day-leg sale filling. All PDT day-trade budget then stays free for emergency same-day de-risking.
caveats: Daily bars stand in for intraday execution. The open stands in for the 09:32 entry, the close for the 15:49 exit, and the TP is judged on the daily high, which can include prints before the entry. Calibration against 21 one-minute sessions, 40 five-minute sessions and 12 live legs supports +0.15% entry slip as realistic. The optimistic scenario (entry = open) is shown alongside, and even it is about zero or negative over every long sample.

Dataset C's overnight leg is synthetic (2x NVDA close->open minus 4bp), not NVDL. NVDA earnings dates for 2018-2024 were entered from memory; as a check, the mean |NVDA gap| on those nights is 5.05% vs 1.19% on other nights. Dataset B drops NVDL before 2023-07 because of bad opening prints and replaces the 2023-12-27 distribution night with 2x NVDA.

Overnight exposure is fixed at 0.89 of E (fractional). PAUSE exposure is 1 NVDL share at $36.58, and TZA is held at $48.26 for the whole-share variants. Real share-count granularity and price drift are not modelled. The rotating 3-on/2-off schedule ignores holidays.
The rolling-20 high uses end-of-day marks only. PAUSE is checked at 09:31 and at end of day. Live monitoring may differ, for example intraday marks or a different restart rule after the 5 sessions.

Block bootstrap with block 5 and a fixed seed. Monte Carlo se is about 0.6 points on a 20% probability and about 0.003-0.004%/session on log growth. It cannot represent regimes longer than the sample, and the 1y sample holds only 4 NVDA earnings nights.

A real recent regime would change the verdict. Over the last 30 sessions the day leg made +0.62%/day, and the breakeven mean is only about +0.03-0.05%/day. Persistent positive alpha would favour a modest leg. But no long sample (1y, 3.3y, 8.8y) shows it, and under realistic execution the mean is negative in every calendar year 2018-2026.
The amplifier correlation (+0.12 to +0.16) holds only in 2023-2026. Over 2017-2026 it is about zero. Treat the amplification as regime-dependent; the growth and PAUSE conclusions do not depend on it.
Selecting the best of 5 inverse ETFs was not tested over the long sample (only TZA history was fetched). That selection step can only inflate the trailing score further.

reports.lens: LIVE VS MODEL: 12 live TZA day legs (T3X-D01..D12, 9/17-10/12) checked against same-session models (daily open->close, the daily TP rule, and 1-minute TP models), plus execution cost, inference on the true mean, and whether +$3.23 is consistent with zero edge
key_findings: Live record. P&L recomputed from qty x (exit - entry) is +$3.236, which matches state.realised_total 3.23. Return on position: mean +0.341%/leg, sd 0.928, median +0.445, 7 of 12 wins (58%), average win +1.006%, average loss -0.591%. As % of prior-close equity: mean +0.274%/leg. The 12 legs mix two rules. Legs 1-5 were hold-to-15:49: mean +0.162%, 2 of 5 wins. Legs 6-12 used the 1% TP: mean +0.469%, sd 0.797, 5 of 7 wins. Only legs 6-12 are out-of-sample for the TP, which was tuned on 9/28 over a window that includes legs 1-5.

Pure execution is clean. Entry vs the OHLC4 of the minute the order was sent: +0.017% (sd 0.083). Exit at 15:49 vs the 15:48 bar close: -0.010% (8 close-outs, sd 0.038). Vs the 15:49 bar open: -0.009%. TP fills came at the limit price. With the actual live entry price, the 1-minute model reproduces live to -0.006%/leg (sd 0.031) and gets all 7 of 7 TP outcomes right (4 hits, 3 misses). Order-handling slippage is about 0.03% per round trip, roughly $0.02-0.03 per leg on about $88 notional.

Models are much more optimistic than live on the same sessions, under the rule in force each day. Frictionless 1-minute model (entry at the 09:31 close, exit at the 15:48 close): +0.683%/leg vs live +0.341%, a gap of -0.342%/leg (median -0.10). In dollars that gap is -$3.84 of a $7.07 model total. Two legs account for -$3.12 of it. On 9/28 the entry was +0.15% above the 09:31 close and the TP sat 2c above the post-entry high. On 10/9 the entry was +0.25% above and the TP sat 7c above. Daily-bar model under the rule in force: +0.788%/leg, gap -0.447. On the TP legs alone the daily-model gap is -0.239%/leg; on the hold legs it is -0.739 (entries averaged +0.22% above the 09:30 open).

TP hits, model vs live (7 TP legs): live 4 of 7. 1-minute model with live entry: 4 of 7. 1-minute model with entry at the 09:31 close + 0.01 (as in the tptest script): 6 of 7. Daily-bar model: 5 of 7. Applying the TP after the fact to all 12 legs: live-entry 1m 8 of 12, 09:31-close model 10 of 12, daily 10 of 12.

The modelled TP edge depends heavily on the exact entry price. Over the 21 sessions in the 1m file, the TP-rule mean is +0.826% at an entry of the 09:31 close. Shifting the entry up by +0.10% gives +0.721, +0.15% gives +0.562, and +0.30% gives +0.480. A realistic entry (09:32 bar OHLC4 + 0.017%) gives +0.665, an expected cost of about -0.16%/leg. Applying the 12 observed live entry offsets gives -0.117%/leg. The +0.82% figure from the 10/13 OCO-TP study is an in-sample optimum.

Inference on 12 legs: t = 1.27 on return (two-sided p 0.229, one-sided 0.115) and t = 1.14 on dollars (p 0.277). 95% t-interval for the true mean: [-0.249, +0.931]%/leg; bootstrap 95% CI [-0.151, +0.851]; bootstrap P(mean <= 0) = 0.092. In dollars: 95% CI [-0.25, +0.79] per leg. Wilcoxon p 0.204; sign test for 7/12 p 0.387. TP legs alone: t = 1.56, one-sided p 0.085, 95% CI [-0.268, +1.206].

+$3.23 is fully consistent with zero true edge. Drawing 12 legs at live notionals from a zero-mean version of the 1-year daily TP-rule distribution (sd 1.92, skew -1.89) gives P(sum >= +$3.24) = 0.319. The 90% null range is -$10.60 to +$8.69. With the live entry offset applied, P = 0.338. By contrast, the 1m frictionless model's own distribution puts the live total at P(sum <= $3.24) = 0.003. The 1m model is rejected as a live forecast; zero edge is not.

The live sample has not yet seen the tail. In the 1-year daily TP distribution, P(leg < -1%) = 0.217 and P(leg < -2%) = 0.155. Legs below -2% contribute -0.617%/day to the mean; the rest average +0.696. The worst live leg was -0.90%. P(no leg below -1% in 12 draws) = 0.053 (0.031 with the live entry offset). So the live sd of 0.93 understates risk. Using the 1-year sd, the standard error is 0.554 and the 95% CI widens to [-0.744, +1.426].

Long-run baseline (TZA, 258 sessions to 10/9, recomputed). Open->close: +0.035%/day, sd 2.946. Daily TP rule entering at the open: -0.029%, sd 1.918, skew -1.89, hit rate 70.5% (this confirms the critic's figure). Entering at open + 0.218% (the live average offset): -0.224%, hit rate 66.7%. Recent windows: last 64 sessions +0.313%, last 30 +0.637%; first 194 sessions -0.141%.

Selection and regime check: the score that picked TZA (trailing 30-session open->close mean/sd) correlates 0.033 with the next 12 sessions' daily TP mean, across 216 overlapping windows. Only 6.1% of rolling 30-session windows score >= 0.45. The current window is a rare regime, not a persistent trait.

Posteriors for the true mean (%/leg) combining the live data with a normal prior:
- 1-year daily TP prior: +0.032 (sd 0.109), P(mu > 0) = 0.62; with the 1-year sd, -0.013, P = 0.46.
- 1-year prior with live entry offset: -0.114, P = 0.17; with the 1-year sd, -0.194, 95% [-0.445, +0.058], P = 0.07.
- Skeptical N(0, 0.30): +0.190, P = 0.83.

Only priors built on the selection window give P > 0.97, and those are contaminated by selection: last-64 prior +0.320 (95% [+0.050, +0.591]); 1m model prior +0.588.

Power: to detect mu = 0.34%/leg at 80% power (one-sided 5%) takes 46 legs if sd is 0.93, or 197 if sd is 1.92. For mu = 0.2: 134 or 570 legs. At about 3 legs a week, live trading will not settle the question within the 6-12 month horizon.

Conclusion for this lens: execution is not leaking. The live shortfall against the models comes from model optimism: entry convention plus the TP threshold. The live result cannot be told apart from zero, and realistic long-run evidence centres on about 0 to -0.2%/leg. The 1m model with real entries replicates live outcomes almost exactly, so a shadow log produces the same evidence as live legs without taking about 90% of equity into a negatively skewed intraday bet.

recommended_changes: Suspend the live day leg. In its place, keep a daily shadow log: record the real 09:32 ask and the order time, then score the TP/15:49 outcome from 1-minute bars. This analysis shows the 1m model with the real entry matches live to -0.006%/leg and 7/7 on TP outcomes, so the shadow log produces the same evidence with no capital at risk.

Re-enable only with a written criterion. Shadow plus live legs should reach at least 40 with a mean above 0 at t >= 2, scored with a realistic entry (09:32-09:33 fill, not the 09:31 close or the daily open). The sample should also include at least one small-cap up-trend regime and at least one leg below -2%, so the tail is represented.

If the operator keeps the leg anyway, cut it to about 45% of equity rather than about 90%. The modelled edge is about zero and the tail (legs below -2%, which cost -0.62%/day in the 1-year data) drives the PAUSE risk. Also write the live-model haircut into §11's expected value: -0.16%/leg vs the 1m frictionless model and about -0.24%/leg vs the daily TP model on TP legs. The current '+0.3% of E per active day' is not supported.

Do not re-tune the TP to recover the 9/28 and 10/9 misses (for example, by moving to 0.75%). A 0.15% entry shift moves the 21-session mean from +0.83 to +0.56, so the threshold is fitted to the sample. Any re-test should use 1m bars with 09:32 OHLC4 + 0.02% entries and data outside the 9/14-10/12 tuning window.

Fix the records, and do not let the review cite pct fields from trades.csv. In the DAY rows, column 16/17 order flips: D01-D03 are pnl then pct, D04-D12 are pct then pnl. D01's recorded 'pct' of 1.83 is P&L divided by equity, not the position return (2.09%). D08's state entry is missing qty and pct. Recompute any review from prices.
caveats: n = 12 legs in a single 4-week regime of small-cap intraday weakness. Every interval is wide, and the live sd (0.93) is probably too low, since no leg fell below -1%. That had about a 5% chance under the 1-year distribution.

The 1-minute file covers only 21 sessions (9/14-10/12), and the 10/1 TP fill (09:40:54) shows up in the 1m bars only at 09:41, so the bars are not perfect tick-level truth. The daily file ends 10/9, so the 10/12 daily bar was rebuilt from 1m bars (open = first 1m open).

The long-run baseline is daily bars, which overstate TP hits because the high can print before the entry. The live-offset version (-0.224%) is a rough correction. The critic's 7.8-year synthetic -3x IWM figure (+0.02%/day) was not recomputed here.

Live legs 1-5 ran a different rule (hold to 15:49). Applying the TP to them after the fact is in-sample, because the TP was chosen on 9/28 over a window that includes them. Only 7 legs are true out-of-sample tests of the current rule.
Equity-based returns use the prior day's 16:02 equity, not the cash at 09:32 after the overnight exit. The 10/1 leg was under-sized (1 share, 47% of equity) under the pre-v1.4 sizing.
Regulatory sell fees (SEC/TAF) are not in the recorded P&L and were not verified from broker data. At this size they are probably about $0.01-0.02 per leg, which does not change any conclusion.

Suspension is a risk-management call that rests on the long-run prior and the tail. If the current small-cap-weakness regime persists, the leg's recent-window expectation is positive (last-64 prior posterior +0.32%/leg), and suspending it gives up that upside.

reports.lens: MECHANISM & ALTERNATIVES FOR THE PDT SLOTS: is there a structural reason for a positive open->close drift in -3x small caps, and is TZA the best use of the 3 PDT slots a week? Tested on 16.8 years of daily bars (2010-01 to 2026-10-13) for IWM, SPY, QQQ, TZA, TNA, SQQQ, SPXS, SOXS, TQQQ, UPRO and SPXL. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/wf2/mechanism/ (decomp.py, letf.py, sim2.py, rank.py, extra.py, long3x.py, cadence.py, biascheck.py).
key_findings: The structural premise is not supported. IWM's open->close arithmetic mean over 2010-2026 is -0.0027%/day (t -0.16, n 4218), close to zero. The overnight mean is +0.047%/day (t +3.71). The familiar 'small caps lose intraday' result holds only in compounded/log terms: the sum of IWM intraday log returns is -37.8%, against +184% overnight. That comes from variance (-sigma^2/2), not from a negative arithmetic drift. A daily-reset -3x holder earns about -3x the arithmetic drift, so there is nothing to harvest.

By sub-period, IWM intraday drift is +0.016%/day (t +0.54) for 2010-15, -0.008 (t -0.27) for 2016-20, -0.017 (t -0.55) for 2021-26 and -0.004 (t -0.10) for 2024-26. No period is significant, and the sign flips from year to year. In 9 of 17 years it was negative.

The large-cap mirror has the opposite sign. SPY intraday is +0.023%/day (t +1.83) and QQQ +0.027%/day (t +1.73). So -3x large-cap inverse ETFs have a structurally negative intraday drift. Measured SQQQ open->close is -0.108%/day (t -2.28) and SPXS -0.092%/day (t -2.41), 2010-2026.

Expected -3x intraday drift. A model of TZA built from IWM bars, -3*i*(1+g)/(1-3g), gives +0.0070%/day over the full sample. The convexity term is only -0.0007%/day, so there is no meaningful intraday volatility drag inside the ETF. Actual TZA open->close is -0.039%/day (t -0.74) because TZA's opening print averages 0.046%/day rich to IWM-implied fair value (t -3.3); that is -0.008%/day over 2024-26. Actual TZA was +0.033%/day (t +0.36) for 2021-26 and +0.020%/day (t +0.16) for 2024-26.

The 'mirror' thesis in RULES_v3 §11 is false. Compounded intraday-only returns over the full sample were -88.9% for TNA and -98.6% for TZA; over the last 2 years, -19.0% and -22.1%. The long and the inverse both lose intraday when compounded. A 2x long losing intraday therefore does not imply that the inverse wins.

The volatility drag that matters is the account's own. Compounding a 90% TZA position gives gross growth of E[log(1+0.9r)]: -0.0207%/active day for hold-to-close vs an arithmetic +0.0298 (2021-26), a drag of 0.050%/day. With the 1% TP the drag is 0.017%/day.

The TZA day leg (TP 1% else close, on daily bars) is at or below zero in every window, even gross of costs: -0.067%/day (t -2.12) for 2010-26, -0.027 (t -0.70) for 2016-26, -0.008 (t -0.14) for 2021-26, -0.017 (t -0.19) for the last 2 years and -0.051 (t -0.41) for the last year. With 0.03% slippage on each side it is -0.036 to -0.103%/day. The rule's expected +0.30%/day is rejected at t -11.7 (full sample), -5.8 (2021-26) and -3.7 (last 2 years).

The 1% TP does not create edge over the long sample. TZA hold-to-close vs TP1 gross: +0.008 vs -0.027 (2016-26), +0.033 vs -0.008 (2021-26). The TP lowers the mean by about 0.03%/day; it only reshapes the distribution (sd 3.4% -> 2.1%, skew about -2). The TP's win in the 21- and 30-session studies is specific to that sample.

Alternative (a), SQQQ or SPXS: both are worse than TZA in every multi-year window, gross. SQQQ TP1: -0.083 (full), -0.086 (2016-26), -0.115 (2021-26), -0.155 (last 2y). SPXS TP1: -0.084, -0.064, -0.088, -0.100. At 3 of 5 days and 90% size, that is about -8.7% to -15.6% a year of account equity gross (2016-26 / 2021-26), vs TZA's -1.0% to -3.6%.

Alternative (b), TZA+SQQQ basket: worse and close to infeasible. Mean TP1 gross is -0.072 (full), -0.057 (2016-26), -0.061 (2021-26), -0.086 (last 2y). Intraday correlation is 0.73 (full) and 0.76 (last 2y), so the diversification is small. Each symbol's round trip is its own day trade, so the basket uses 2 of the 3 rolling slots per day: about 1 basket day per 5, or 1.5 if a single-symbol leg uses the third slot. Whole-share sizing at about $105: 1 TZA ($48.26) + 1 SQQQ ($33.99) = $82.25, which is 78% of equity, weighted 59/41. Equal weight is not achievable.

Alternative (c), cash: 0%/day. That beats TZA on gross expectation in every window except two hold-to-close windows (2021-26 +0.033 and last 2y +0.008, both t < 0.4). After realistic costs, cash beats every inverse variant in every window tested.

Mirror alternative tested out of curiosity: long 3x large caps intraday. Gross hold-to-close is +0.065 to +0.074%/day (t about 1.6-1.7, full sample) for UPRO, SPXL and TQQQ, but about +0.004 to +0.014%/day (t <= 0.3) after realistic costs. The TP rule makes them negative. There is no tradable structural edge on either side.

The trailing-30 ranking has no predictive value. Weekly rank-and-hold-#1 (TP1, gross) averaged -0.096%/day on active days, 2010-26 (t -1.78). Days when TZA was picked averaged -0.068%/day, against -0.047 when it was not. In non-overlapping blocks, the correlation of TZA's trailing-30 score with its next-20-session mean is -0.14 (207 blocks): mean reversion, not persistence. TZA's 30-session score of 0.450 into 2026-10-09 (mean +0.778%, win 73%) sits in the top 0.6% of all 30-day TZA windows since 2010 (0.7% for the best of the 4 ETFs). That is selection on an extreme outlier.

The recent edge is a regime, not a structure. TZA hold by month in 2026: Jan -0.62, Apr -0.91, Jul +0.63, Sep +0.90%/day, tracking IWM intraday (Jan +0.22, Apr +0.33, Sep -0.30%/day). TZA hold for 2026 overall is +0.005%/day.

Live check: 12 day legs (D01-D12) averaged +0.341%/leg (sd 0.93, t +1.27, sum +4.09%). Live trailed the daily-bar simulation on the same dates by 0.38%/leg, mostly because 09:32 fills on D01-D06 sat 0.3-1.0% above the open. On overlapping intraday data, the daily-bar TP simulation was optimistic vs a 09:32 entry by 0.015%/day (1-minute bars, 21 sessions) and by 0.124%/day vs a 09:35 entry (5-minute bars, 40 sessions). The long-sample daily-bar results are therefore more likely optimistic than pessimistic.

Risk added: the day leg alone at 3 of 5 days and 90% size, over 60-session windows in 2021-26 (gross TZA TP1): median -0.04%, 5th percentile -16.7%, P(max drawdown >= 10%) 49.9%, P(max drawdown >= 20%) 8.1%. With realistic costs: median -1.04%, P(max drawdown >= 20%) 9.3%. It adds drawdown risk of PAUSE size with no expected return.

recommended_changes: Suspend the RULES_v3 §11 day leg and hold cash 09:32-15:49. No structural edge exists (IWM arithmetic intraday drift is about 0), its long-sample expectation is at or below 0 even gross of costs, and it adds roughly 8-10% probability of a 20% day-leg drawdown over 60 sessions.

Do not replace TZA with SQQQ or SPXS. Large-cap intraday drift is positive (SPY +0.023, QQQ +0.027%/d), so -3x large caps are structurally negative intraday (-0.06 to -0.15%/d gross). Do not adopt the TZA+SQQQ basket: it is worse on mean, its correlation is 0.73-0.76, it uses 2 day trades per day, and equal weight is not achievable in whole shares at about $105.

Keep the 3 PDT slots unused as an emergency reserve for the overnight leg, for example a same-day exit after a 15:52 fill error or a late shock. This also removes the 09:31 -> 09:32 -> 15:49 -> 15:52 cash-chaining dependency, where a stuck day-leg order can under-size the overnight entry.

Retire the trailing-30 inverse-ETF ranking for the day leg. Out of sample it has negative predictive value (corr -0.14; picked days did worse than unpicked), and the current TZA score of 0.45 is a top-0.6% outlier, most likely to mean-revert.

Correct the §11 thesis text. The 'mirror' claim is false: TNA and TZA both lose intraday when compounded (-88.9% and -98.6% full sample). The '+0.3% of E per active day' expectation is rejected at t -3.7 to -11.7.

If the operator wants to keep testing, use paper only. Log the hypothetical TZA 09:32 entry, TP 1% else 15:49 result each eligible day, with no orders. Reinstate only on a pre-registered out-of-sample pass, for example 60 shadow legs with t > 2, which needs a mean of about 0.54%/d. Otherwise, at most 1 share (about 45% of equity) with a hard stop on the experiment after 20 legs if the mean is <= 0.
caveats: Daily bars approximate the live 09:32 entry with the opening print, and the TP fill with the day's high (with +1c fill-through), so intrabar ordering is ignored. On the sessions with overlapping intraday data the daily simulation was optimistic (by 0.015%/d on 1-minute bars, 0.124%/d on 5-minute bars, and 0.38%/leg on the 12 live legs). Over the 16-year sample the bias direction is unverified.
Costs are assumed at 0.03% each side, against live marketable limits capped at ask + max(0.02, 0.15%). Real costs could be higher, which strengthens the verdict.
Prices are split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted. Overnight means for SPY and IWM are understated by about the dividend yield (roughly 0.005-0.007%/d); intraday results are unaffected.

2010 TZA data shows a large open premium (-0.36%/d actual minus model) that may be a data artifact. The conclusions hold on 2016-26 and 2021-26 alone. SOXS volume data is missing for 2478 days; prices were used as given.

Leveraged-ETF close-of-day rebalancing and intraday momentum (Cheng-Madhavan, Baltussen et al.) were not tested: no long intraday sample was fetched. That effect depends on the day's direction and cannot produce an unconditional positive -3x drift, but a conditional momentum rule is unexplored.

Literature references (Cliff-Cooper-Gulen 2008, Kelly-Clark 2011, Berkman et al. 2012, Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019) are cited from memory, not checked in this session. The empirical tests above stand on their own.

A persistent regime of small-cap intraday weakness (as in Jul-Oct 2026) cannot be ruled out ex ante. The 16-year data show no persistence in 30 -> 20 session intraday means, so the regime cannot be identified in time to trade it.

The 60-session drawdown statistics use the running maximum within each window, not the exact rolling-20-high PAUSE rule, and leave out the overnight leg. The interaction with the overnight leg was covered by the earlier critic (about 5% -> about 20% P(PAUSE) in 60 nights).

Sample-size limits: even 2 years of data give a 95% CI for TZA TP1 of [-0.19, +0.15]%/d. A small positive edge of about 0.05%/d cannot be excluded, but it would be too small to cover costs, drag and the PAUSE risk it adds.

judge.rationale:
All five lenses recommend suspending the day leg. I re-ran the disputed numbers from the raw files (scripts j1-j5.py in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-test-trading/0c00e7d9-c916-50ae-ac83-8f6429819f25/scratchpad/wf2/judge/), and they back the verdict.

1. The thesis is false. IWM's arithmetic open->close drift is about zero:
   - 2000-2026: -0.007%/d (t -0.43). 2010-2026: -0.002%/d. 2021-2026: -0.017%/d. Last 2 years: +0.004%/d.
   - IWM's return comes overnight: +0.047% to +0.068%/d.
   - A daily-reset -3x position therefore has no intraday drift to harvest. The 'mirror' claim in §11 does not hold.

2. The 1% TP rule on TZA daily bars is at or below zero in every long window.
   - Entry at the open (0 slip): 2008+ -0.057%/d (t -1.8); 2010+ -0.061%; 2011-07+ -0.010%; 2016+ -0.022%; 2021+ +0.002%; last 2y 0.000%; last 1y -0.016%.
   - With 0.1% entry cost: -0.10% to -0.17%/d in every window (2008+ -0.161%, t -5.0).
   - The reviewers' conflicting long-sample figures (-0.010, -0.062 and -0.162) are all correct. They differ only by start date and slippage assumption.
   - The TP raises the win rate to about 70% and makes skew about -2.5. It does not add expectancy.
   - The positive figures come only from recent windows: last 30 sessions +0.61%, last 60 +0.36%, last 120 +0.21%. Over the last 250 sessions it is -0.14%.

3. The execution haircut is real. I re-checked it on the 21 one-minute sessions:
   - Daily-bar or open-entry model: +0.82-0.85%. Entry at the 09:31 close: +0.826%. Entry at the 09:32 bar (where live fills actually land): +0.667%.
   - That is a cost of about 0.16%/leg, and open->09:32 drift was +0.20%.
   - So the lens finding of '0.015 optimism' used the 09:31 close; the finding of '0.16-0.18' used the 09:32 bar. The 09:32 figure is the right one.

4. A gate does not rescue it.
   - Trailing-30 mean>0, next-day TP (2011-07+, 0 slip): ON -0.048% vs OFF +0.025%. That is backwards.
   - Score >= 0.4, excluding the current run: 29 days in about 15 years in 6 episodes, mean +0.31% at 0 slip and +0.05% at 0.1% (t <= 1). It fires about twice a year and is not significant.
   - Score >= 0.3: n=105, +0.04% / -0.07%.

5. Risk and growth (my joint 1y block bootstrap, 5000 paths; I approximated earnings nights as cash).
   - P(PAUSE within 60 sessions): 4.5% overnight-only; 18.0% with the 90% leg at an open entry and 23.7% at a realistic +0.15% entry; 8.3% / 9.9% with 1 share.
   - Over 125 sessions: 10.8% overnight-only vs 36-47% with the 90% leg.
   - Log growth per session falls at every size: 0.307 overnight-only vs 0.278 / 0.187 at 90%, and 0.296 / 0.252 with 1 share.
   - This matches joint-risk (5.1% -> 22.8-27.2%). For the goal of reaching $200, the leg lowers both median and 5th-percentile equity.

6. The live record cannot settle the question.
   - 12 legs: +0.341%/leg, sd 0.93, t 1.27, $+3.24. The 7 TP-era legs: +0.469%, t 1.56.
   - That is consistent with zero edge: P(sum >= $3.24 | zero mean) is about 0.32 per the live lens.

The v1.2 10-day review passed (mean > 0), so this change does not react to a drawdown. It rests on the long-sample evidence that the thesis is false and that live fills cost more than the models assumed.

Suspend beats gate or resize. No condition I or the reviewers could pre-register has a positive out-of-sample mean. Even 1 share costs about 0.01-0.05%/session of log growth and roughly doubles short-horizon PAUSE risk, for an expected return at or below zero.

A shadow log scored at the real 09:32 price is free. It does not use the PDT budget, and the live lens showed it matches live outcomes almost exactly (-0.006%/leg, 7 of 7 TP outcomes).

The decision to suspend the day leg holds. I spot-checked the three numbers it rests on, using data I fetched myself plus the files on disk, and all three match the judge.

(1) Long-sample TP rule on 4,510 TZA daily bars, fetched fresh 2008-11..2026-10-13. Zero slip: 2008+ -0.058%/d (t -1.85), 2011-07+ -0.011, 2021+ -0.001, last 250 -0.027. 0.1% slip: -0.162 (t -5.00), -0.117, -0.104, -0.146. Last 30 sessions +0.626 / +0.607. Hit rate 70.5%, skew -2.83. IWM open->close is about 0 (2008-11+ +0.0007, t 0.04; 2021+ -0.017) and overnight about +0.047%/d, which confirms the thesis is false.

(2) Execution haircut on the 21 one-minute sessions: entry at the 09:31 close gives +0.826% (18 hits), the 09:32 close +0.666% (16 hits), the 09:32 OHLC4 x 1.0002 +0.668%. Open->09:32 drift is +0.238% (t 2.4).

(3) Joint risk, my own 1y block bootstrap (5,000 paths, block 5). P(PAUSE within 60 sessions) goes from 4.4% to 18.1% (zero slip) or 24.5% (0.15% slip) with the 90% leg, and to 8.0% / 9.4% with 1 share. Log growth per session goes from 0.307 to 0.286 / 0.195 (90% leg) and 0.299 / 0.253 (1 share). Keeping every night instead of the judge's 'top-4 gaps = earnings' heuristic, or starting from the real 107.11 HWM, changes these by only 1-3 points. Live: 12 legs average +0.341% (sd 0.928, t 1.27, $3.236).

Gaps, none of which would change the decision:
- The suspension is labelled 'v1.5', but RULES_v3 is already v1.6; it should be v1.7.
- About 130 suspect TZA bars in 2009-2010 drag the 2008+ means down. The rule text should cite the 2011-07+ figures instead (-0.011 at zero slip, -0.117 at 0.1%).
- 'Negative' vs 'about zero' depends on the slip assumption, which is partly the current regime's drift. Long-run expectation is better stated as about 0 to slightly negative. Since breakeven is +0.03-0.05%/d, the leg still fails.
- The status block quotes only the 1y PAUSE numbers; the 3.3y and 8.8y increments are smaller relative to their higher baselines.
- Approval governance is inconsistent: the leg is skipped without sign-off, while the v1.6 overnight change went in the same day without approval either.
- The re-entry criteria are effectively permanent and should say so.

A quick gap-conditional test of the TP rule was negative on both sides. Opening-auction entry and intraday-momentum variants were not tested, but they would be new strategies rather than a rescue of §11.
